:::{#exm-big-o}
#### The function $3n + 5$ is big-O of $n$

Let $f(n) = 3n + 5$ and $g(n) = n$.
To show $f(n) = O(g(n))$ by @def-big-o,
choose $c = 4$ and $N = 5$.
For every [natural number](number-systems.qmd#def-natural-numbers) $n \ge 5$,

$$
\ba
|f(n)|
&= 3n + 5
&& \text{(} 3n + 5 > 0 \text{)}
\\
&\le 3n + n
&& \text{(} 5 \le n \text{, since } n \ge 5 \text{)}
\\
&= 4n
&& \text{(} 3n + n = 4n \text{)}
\\
&= 4 \, |g(n)|,
&& \text{(} n = |n| \text{, since } n \ge 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

which is the [inequality](proof-writing.qmd#def-inequality) in @def-big-o with $c = 4$.
Hence $3n + 5 = O(n)$.

:::
